notes.title: Happy Birthday, Cyber Ops!
notes.content:
It's May 21st, which marks the first anniversary of Cyber Ops since our release in 2020!

It's been a crazy year for the world and for us too. We even released the game during the first months of quarantine, working frome home, just barely adapting to the new reality of the pandemics.

Despite all the difficulties, and in a process not exempt from mistakes and difficult times, we managed to release our first Steam game to the world. 

The lessons we learned are invaluable, and we will apply them in all our future projects. We would love to add some more cool stuff for Cyber Ops (or maybe a sequel/prequel?), with all the knowledge we have today.  Oh man, it would be such an awesome thing!... but only time will tell if the conditions are met to work on something like this. In the meantime, we will continue supporting our community with updates and improvements. Most of them, not so visible, but we have been refactoring many aspects of the game to make it more stable and friendly with our players. 

What's the future of Cyber Ops? We can't say right now, but the first iteration of this crazy concept is here, and thanks to your support and encouragement, we have seen there is a lot of love for this kind of weird, uncommon, game styles. 

We would like to thank our development team, our publishers Games Operatores, and our players... YES, YOU GUYS!! You rock!!! Thanks for helping us create this dark world of cyber black ops we dreamed of.

Oh! And well, there's a juicy discount these days, so if you have a friend who's doubtful about joining the ranks of the Geist Unit, let them know it's their chance to get the latest version of Cyber Ops with all the improvements we have introduced over our first year of life <3

Take care, stay safe, and keep being awesome!!

Sincerely,
Julio @OctetoStudios

notes.title: New Controls Update coming to Beta soon
notes.content:
Hello operators!

It's been a while since our last update, so here's some news for you :)

Over the time Cyber Ops has been live and open to a larger number of players like you (yes, you champ!), we have been analyzing all the feedback and trying to improve different aspects of the game in order to make your playing experience better.

Launching your first original title as a studio is a tough process, but we have learned so many lessons thanks to your help and support. For that, we are grateful for every single comment on the Steam forums, Discord, Twitter, Instagram, etc., as you guys are helping us not only improve Cyber Ops, but to deliver much better games in the future.

For those who wonder, our studio also makes tailor-made games for different clients, and that's how we've kept the lights on for all these years, and that's why we are not lightning-fast when it comes to addressing every single bug and UX issues in the game. 

However, starting with Cyber Ops, we really want to put more focus on creating original games for PC and consoles. We feel it's our duty to keep going and to make good use of all the new knowledge and experience we have gained during the life cycle of Cyber Ops. We will strive to bring progressively better gaming experiences to you every single day.

[b]Anyway, I could go on further, but let's save some more deep reflections for another time :P
[/b]
Now, straight to the point... Cyber Ops original control scheme, inputs and navigation was mostly designed as a way to reinforce the feeling of dettachment from your squad. The game tells you that your mission is to guide and take care of this squad, but we wanted you to feel that you could only do so much about it (for some spoilery reasons). There was not a direct connection between you, the Operator, and the agents, as in "go here exactly" or "do that precisely". There is an intentional gap between your instructions and the agents reaction, because we wanted the agents to feel like separate individuals, and that's why the objective-based navigation feels unnatural and even uncomfortable.

Well... that was our take and it was worth the shot. Maybe it didn't work out so well :P

We tried to do some crazy experimental stuff, but we didn't test enough with new players. Instead, we had a group of testers who eventually got used to how the game works, which didn't let us see that the first time user experience was going to be tougher than we thought.

It may sound logic to you, but we realized it is more important to have a pleasant, smooth experience than sticking to a rigid expressive intention, even if it makes sense because of the story or whatever.

So, in order to reduce unnecessary friction, we are about to roll out a new update with a more classic control-scheme to move your agents around. 

Objectives and tasks remain the same, but the creation method is absolutely straight-forward: a classic one-click = go-here.

We also added the ability to pan the camera around by placing the mouse cursor at the edge of the screen, which comes in handy when you are busy setting up sniper shots, supply drops and you don't want to click again just to scroll the map.

It may not sound as too much, but all of this comes with adapting all the tutorials, in all languages, to help new players get onboard.

This, plus other new "less visible" improvements will be rolled out to the Open Beta branch, so you can test it and share any feedback with us before we officially release the new patch on the main branch of the game.

Sorry about the long post. Do you agree with our thoughts here? Let me know what you guys think in the comments. 

Stay safe, and thanks again for being awesome.

Julio.-
Octeto Studios

notes.title: Need help with hacking?
notes.content:
Hey there Operators!

It seems that the hacking mechanic is a bit cloudy at the moment. This is a quick tutorial so you can keep progressing in the game.

Your main tool to interact with entities and enemies is your Hacking Console. The Console is an "enabler": it allows to affect enemies and entities in different ways.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/69b247317e9720c5622df12eaca869cf1bab230a.jpg[/img]
This is the Console. You need to right click on an enemy or entity, or press the assigned key, to bring it up. It will show the ID of the device or enemy on its upper left corner. That is important!

------------------------------------------------------------
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/3e0d8bd061acd95396e4621dd107409e50b660be.jpg[/img]
Starting from Affect, you need to move the cursor to the right of the console, using the WASD keys (or whatever you assigned to console navigation).

- At the start of the process, you need to enable level 1 hacking in the command column.
- In the Device column, you need to match the data with the current [b]ID[/b] of the device being hacked.
- After that, you can run the process and the device or enemy will be hacked. [u]But only at level 1[/u].

REMEMBER! You can use run+[A] to automatically open a new Console to quickly increase the hack level.

------------------------------------------------------------
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/0e040da1eec5df3f064b6f4fe351bd62cac655b6.jpg[/img]
In order to have access to more powerful tools, you need to go [u]beyond level 1 hacking:[/u] 
Access the hacking console again, on the same device. This time, from Affect, go to [b]enable.L2[/b], match the device ID and run the process.

------------------------------------------------------------
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/3d59b42d561d62bf5293448da58ee4613760a648.jpg[/img]
Now you have Level 2 hacking on this device, and new options to Affect are available. 

------------------------------------------------------------
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/7cfd9b314f96dc320932500c369fa11532c4acf3.jpg[/img]
You can repeat the process until you reach Level 3 hacking.

------------------------------------------------------------
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/f98ea4010bd02a541ac3e42e99c6627c56da90f3.jpg[/img]
Now you have available all Affect processes for this specific system or enemy.

------------------------------------------------------------
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/1f55a7d0a02625bc6a6eeb1a878f0eae9940be21.jpg[/img]
Remember! If you don't want to speed up things, you can always choose to go to the next hacking level through the Device Panel, using the highlighted button on the system. Sometimes, it's faster this way, since you don't have to look for the device inside the current level.

We are working on making this information easier to understand in the game, as well as other difficulty adjustments to make your experience smoother.

Thanks again for your support!!!

notes.title: Cyber Ops - RELEASED
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Operators! [/h1]

[h2]We are more than happy to announce that [b]Cyber Ops is out now.[/b] [/h2]

It's been a long journey since our first post here on 7 Jun 2019. 
For the last two years, we have been making this game with hard work and a big passion. Cyber Ops offers an immersive world with memorable characters and a fresh challenge for you to enjoy. All of this was made especially for you, so you can join the Geist Division and live this new experience.

[previewyoutube=XBHGnY8ZDXQ;full]<video>[/previewyoutube]

Become a part of the Geist Division, a secret high-tech unit created by the government to protect the country from all kinds of next-gen threats. You are the eye in the sky, the invisible hand, the cyber ghost, looking after your team over the net.

Features
[list]
[*]More than 6 hours of story missions full of cyberpunk themes, investigation and political intrigue.
[*]Real-time audio feedback from squad leaders brings life to the world of Cyber Ops.
[*]Different hacking mechanics to keep control of doors, security devices and cyberlink-equipped brains.
[*]Squad management: recruit new blood for the infiltration squads.
[*]Research and Development: develop new cyber-implants to improve the agents performance.
[*]Retro-futuristic computer interfaces and dark analog synth-based music inspired by 80's cult movies.
[/list]

Thank You all for being a part of this journey. It's time to reveal out cyberpunk baby :)

Hope you enjoy it!

We know you have been playing the Beta and the Prologue, and we are grateful for all your feedback.

This post is just to let you know that we have been digesting all your comments, suggestions, pains and bug reports and we are working double-time to include as many of these improvements as possible in the full release version.

A few reminders:

[list]
[*]Make sure you are playing the "open_beta" build by selecting the correct branch (in your Steam library, right-click on Cyber Ops, then click properties, go to the BETAS tab, and choose "open_beta"). 
Here's a quick how-to: [url=https://support.steampowered.com/kb_article.php?ref=7021-eiah-8669]https://support.steampowered.com/kb_article.php?ref=7021-eiah-8669[/url]
[*]You are all playing Beta version, untested builds, so you will most likely find some weird stuff. Your role at this stage is absolutely important because we are putting the game under hundreds of eyeballs, so you are seeing things that we as developers might not have seen. notes.title: Human Augmentations
notes.content:
Hello, future Operators! Going crazy already? We are becoming a little bit restless with all the self-isolation, but it’s not like we were too social to begin with… we are kind of nerds. Keep yourselves and your families and friends safe! Wash your hands! Pre-order Cybero… I mean, today we will learn a little bit regarding what allows Geist agents to survive frantic combat: augmentations.

As previously mentioned, Baltia’s cyber industries were well developed prior to the war, and it was one of the main reasons for the NCE to try and completely destroy the independence movement from the start.

Nowadays, augmentations are available for anyone with enough cash to buy them. However, special implants and cyberization items are banned to the public and are used by military special units, like Geist.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/5d50b3e0deeec9361875d98555e87b1a4775295a.png[/img]

One of the most common implants Agents decide to install in their bodies is the Sensor Suit. Based on the Mk.2 Military Cyber Suite, Geist agents are users of the prototype Mk.3 Sensor Suite, which provides an increased range of vision, allowing the detection and engagement of enemies at safer distances, in all light and weather conditions.

For more aggressive Agents, a stronger body is more suitable for CQC and melee fights. The Baltian government issued a request to the Baltian Cyber Industries R&D division to improve the combat proven CAT Servo and Muscle Suit, for special operations usage. The incorporation of new magnetic articulations and nanofibers to the CAT suit resulted in the improved Advanced Combat Suit, offering an increase in weapon accuracy and user strength, without any real compromise.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/f4ce891304df5f3f9f538a94dccc2533cd166588.png[/img]

How do you feel about human "augmenting"? I would personally replace my knees, because they sound like an old rocking chair :D

... (Hey!, psst!... stay tuned. We will have some exciting news soon!)

notes.title: Weapons and Gadgets - GIP-1A Pistol
notes.content:
Greetings from the Geist Unit HQ! 

It has been quite the ride lately, and our team is doing their best to keep everything moving as smoothly as possible. Remember: [u]wash your hands constantly [/u](cybernetic or not) and [u]prefer remote interactions with your fellow Agents[/u] (grade B secure connections are recommended).

Today we will brief you about the issued sidearm for field operations, the [b]GIP-1A[/b]. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/7fe2d1ed8e2a62d46634d6bc8a237da322668269.png[/img]

The [b]GIP-1A (or Grass Impulse Pistol)[/b] is a next gen weapon, intended for [b]CQB combat[/b]. Accuracy is improved thanks to its design: its internals include a recoil dampener, allowing the pistol to go full auto with improved accuracy. Additionally, the unique caseless 9mm L ammo allows the GIP-1A to deliver a considerable impact to targets, while the Adaptive Propellant System (hence the A on its designation) allows the user to automatically convert ammo from supersonic to subsonic, allowing switching to silencers on the go in exchange for stopping power. 

Each field agent is required to equip the standard loadout before deployment, no exceptions allowed. 

[b]So, GAMEPLAY TIP!: [/b]
If you want your agents to go silent, then [i]change the strategy to "Stealth"[/i], and they will immediately switch to the [b]silenced GIP-1A[/b], ready for a well-timed [i]stealth-kill[/i].

notes.title: Weapons and Gadgets - C95U SMG
notes.content:
Another Tuesday, another Devlog! It’s time to meet the main field weapon for Geist Unit agents, the [b]C95U[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/29966d78ab34f8067a4704a68fd60c0ef333ae60.png[/img]

After the war, an in-depth analysis of combat data was requested by the MoD. The idea was to start producing locally developed weapons and war material, since shortages and lack of supplies were key factors in many engagements against the better trained and armed NCE troops. Baltia had to be independent in many areas, including its military industry.

The analysis showed, among other things, the need for a specialized [b]CQC submachine gun[/b], with a high rate of fire and good stopping power. Cyber Industries was assigned to develop a suitable gun for the Baltian Armed Forces.

Based on the reliable C90 SMG in use by the American Empire, the [b]C95U (Ultimate)[/b] is a Baltian specific production model coming from the C90 platform. Never disclosed to the public, the C95U contract was awarded to the Baltian National Armoured Institute. The U model includes a complete internal redesign of the original C90. This redesign allows the weapon to use the newly developed caseless 5.8×25mm ammunition, allowing the C95U to have a larger ammo capacity, while helping in lessening the weight load for the field agent.

What kind of strategy do you plan to use? Fire at will? Stealth?

notes.title: Weapons and Gadgets - The Net Dagger
notes.content:
Hey there, future Operators! We sincerely hope you are safe and well. These are harsh times, but as many times before, the human spirit will prevail. Wash your cyber-hands and stay home if you can!

Today we will talk about the single most important tool of field agents in the world of Cyber-Ops, the incredible [b]Net Dagger[/b].

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/80b44b030dda5a8fc61169e671de0e8cce4be34c.png[/img]

A few years after the end of the war, and with a rise in cyber crime and terrorism, the newly formed Baltian government detected an increased need for a quick tampering and hacking device to be used during field operations. 

With this in mind, the Baltian DoD requested its [b]Cyber Industries R&D division [/b]to design a fitting solution. After several years of trial and error, Cyber Industries delivered the first prototypes of the [b]Digital Warfare Knife (DWK) - Net Dagger[/b] to the DoD to be tested. 

The [b]DWK-1[/b] allows the user to [u]penetrate physical encasings[/u], connecting the targeted terminal remotely with the assigned [b]Operator[/b], allowing him to [u]inject software and hack or control the system[/u].

Compact, resilient, made with cutting edge (pun intended) materials, the [b]Net Dagger [/b]was a game changer for Baltia’s special operatives. The DoD banned its export to other countries, so Baltia is its only global user.

Would you like to have a real-life Net Dagger? 

...me too :D

notes.title: Geopolitical scenario of the game - The Post War Era
notes.content:
Hello Operators! This week we are bringing some more information about Baltia after the war. Enjoy!

In less than a decade, Baltia’s previously weak borders were consolidated by means of an international peacekeeping operation, organized by the [b]AFN (Assembly of Free Nations)[/b], guaranteeing to a certain extent the nonintervention of the [b]NCE [/b]on the internal affairs of Baltia. However, the shielding from the international community over Baltia had an expiration date. The new government of [b]Baltia[/b], knowing that the future of the country was in danger, did not hesitate to initiate an ambitious and never before seen process of modernization of its territory. Thanks to its positive view inside the international community, Baltia was able to obtain large credits and funds, which were put to use in an industrialization process never seen in modern history. The Baltians didn’t want to be absorbed again by the NCE; a strong Baltian consciousness developed among them. Baltians that had fled from the country during the war returned to the country, bringing with them knowledge and money that was put to work towards the development of Baltia.

The AFN peace forces maintained its presence in the country for exactly 10 years. Baltia developed an industry based on the research of advanced software and artificial intelligence, targeting the market of [b]cybernetics [/b]and the new technologies of [b]NInternet[/b]. Its industry focused on [u][b]high tech – high investment – high return products[/b][/u].

While inside the NCE, Baltia was considered its “Silicon Valley”, since many of the new technologies and advances that benefited the NCE industry came from Baltian scientists and companies. In less than 15 years, Baltia was striding further and further ahead of the NCE.

Under the supervision of the AFN, Baltia organized its new [b]Self Defense Forces[/b] in order to be technologically advanced, but limited in their offensive capabilities: the AFN didn’t want future Baltian governments to start a military campaign against the NCE -the independence war was rather brutal and thousand of Baltians soldiers and civilians were killed. However, Baltia's leaders knew that the country would face new battlefields and enemies that conventional armies couldn’t defeat. Located at the frontier between two opposite worlds, Baltia would have to play as a political and military buffer between the NCE and the West.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/5a64ef7a38562146600e630d4a29bc169e033f38.png[/img]

When the time is running out, what kind of hi-tech self-defense unit would you create?

notes.title: Characters and World Context: Egon Daumantas
notes.content:
Hello again, Operators! We sincerely hope that all of you are ok with the current international developments. Here at the Geist HQ we are adapting, taking things seriously and working from home, so we can keep with our normal operations.

Today we will learn a little bit about the [b]big boss[/b] of the Geist Unit, [b]General Egon Daumantas.[/b]

General Daumantas had a key role during the war, gathering support from the international community and openly calling for an intervention at the meetings of the[b] AFN Security Council[/b]. Daumantas was one of the most capable and experienced officers of the Baltian Province and his unit was the first to [b]rebel against the[/b] [b]NCE[/b], openly calling to resist its ruling party.

Although Daumantas wasn’t the mastermind behind the rebellion, he fully supported the cause, and only agreed to step into the public eye due to the desperate situation of the country during the first year of the war.

Presumed [b]KIA [/b]by the media, Daumantas has willingly fallen into the shadows, knowing that future wars will not be fought by armies, but by elite units as Geist.

Tasked by the ECP to create and lead [b]the first Geist Unit[/b], Daumantas has developed a keen sense of duty and strategy. [i]Baltia first, everything else second.[/i] That’s his motto.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/a0819b9a752a401267df2db57819710a8297c6a4.jpg[/img]

See you soon... in the meantime, stay safe and play a lot of games!! :)

notes.title: Geist Division: General facts
notes.content:
After the 5 Years War, the government of [b]Baltia [/b]mandated, under the utmost secrecy, the creation of a Special Operations Command, designated as the [b]Geist Division[/b]. Its main objective: to counter internal and external terrorist threats (both physical and cybernetic). This command was allowed operational freedom, and while technically subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior, it would answer directly to the [b]Emergency Cabinet of the Presidency (ECP)[/b].

The [b]Geist Division[/b] was designed to incorporate four Geist Units. However, lack of funding has only allowed the deployment of one. The unit focuses on flexibility, being able to eliminate threats quickly and silently inside heavily populated areas with an expected low percentage of civilian casualties. In order to improve their efficiency, almost all members of the unit were issued with some type of cybernetic implant or prosthesis, which gave them enhanced capacities both in physical and in cyber combat.

Geist Unit missions will generally be assigned by the ECP, which acquires intel through its own channels. However, the Geist Unit is generally free to conduct its own investigations, as long as they are approved by the Squad Commander, who takes responsibility for the actions of each member. Future deployments of Geist Units are expected to be distributed among the most important cities of Baltia. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/040c6964a480044f2fab9e0b8da2bce12756aeff.png[/img]
[b][i]Geist Division Emblem[/i][/b]

notes.title: Characters and World Context: Hall Borko
notes.content:
[b]Borko [/b]was a computer engineer at one of Baltia’s Weapon Research facilities managed by the [b]NCE [/b]before the war. Just before the war started, Borko was asked by the NCE government to specialize in Nuclear Technologies.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/143837c28da2ce4a0f9cf3279bd3a9af2cc0f285.jpg[/img]

After the [b]Separatists [/b]took over the province, he saw his family suffer due to the subsequent NCE invasion, deciding to join forces with the local militia shortly after the start of the conflict.

Borko has an unmatched ability to [b]snipe targets at long distances[/b]. Raised in a family of hunters, he honed his shooting skills during most of his childhood, pouring all his experience into the war.

Feared by the NCE, he accumulated [b]150 confirmed kills [/b]during the conflict, working several times together with a young but intrepid Ellen.

His records show him as KIA, but it was [b]Daumantas [/b]who asked him to go into the shadows to be part of the Geist Unit.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/30ed28fa6b07f440c4b5f1259413877d49791efd.png[/img]
Operator, you can count with Borko' Sniper Support during the missions by upgrading the Support branch of your skill tree.

notes.title: Geopolitical scenario of the game - The 5-year War
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/8c1a576b562d1132c55839d0c0a3d6b44732ef68.png[/img]

The world begins to recover from a convulsive and violent period, where the power balance between the [b]Erebian nations [/b]and the [b]Eastern giants[/b] was broken. During this time, the biggest Eastern country, the [b]NCE (New Central Empire)[/b], went through a series of independence attempts from several regional states.

Most of these separatist attempts (more political than military-based) were mercilessly crushed, and those involved were treated as mere terrorism, ignoring the historical context and possible justification for said acts. 

Within this scenario, the western world was surprised by the tenacious resistance of a small NCE region, formerly known as [b]Baltia[/b]. 

Baltia went through a harsh war against the NCE, which lasted 5 years. The region was able to resist enough time for the [b]international community[/b] to put enough pressure against the NCE, finally forcing it to recognize the right of the Baltians to become an independent nation.

This was cheered by the Western nations, but it was a huge blow to the NCE aspiration to become a world power.

5 years after the armed conflict, a secret hi-tech unit is born within Baltia... are you ready, Operator?

notes.title: Characters and World Context: Marcus Fox
notes.content:
[h3]Hello there Operators! Today we will meet another field agent of the Geist Unit: [b]Marcus Fox[/b].[/h3]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/611a9cc4f683840ad1cfac0eeaf89623b014dc20.jpg[/img]

Born in [b]Baltia [/b]but raised in the [b]American Empire[/b], Marcus had a happy childhood. His father was a respected member of the Empire´s military, thus Marcus followed his steps. He joined the Army, applying to the [b]Imperial Rangers[/b]. He saw combat in several low key conflicts, until assigned to serve as part of the Quick Reaction Unit created by the [b]Assembly of Free Nations (AFN)[/b] to enforce a no-conflict area in Baltia. 

After witnessing the desperate condition of Baltia’s self-defense forces, he deserted his unit and joined with the local militia, becoming a mercenary. He fought the last 4 years of the war against NCE forces, briefly meeting [b]Ellen [/b]at the battlefield. After the war, the Empire Army charged him with desertion and treason, arresting him. However, [b]General Daumantas[/b] helped in clearing his name: the General was interested in recruiting him from the start. He was selected as a member of the [b]Geist Unit[/b] due to his combat record, as well as for his will to leave everything behind for the sake of Baltia.

[b]Marcus [/b]will usually serve as field leader, specializing in hostage rescue and facility infiltrations. He and Ellen have a special bond, forged in the battlefield as brothers in arms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34265206/87d85669728f7b2edb9ef3cf091730223e0636e0.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Cyber Ops: Cyborgs are real?
notes.content:
Cyborgs are very real! Well, in this world, at least. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/eafbebcd511d86d7f5be4253e878e0c788d218e5.png[/img]

Baltia’s importance for the NCE is two-folded. In order to maintain its local influence, the NCE needed to avoid areas of its territory to go rogue to form an independent country. However, the biggest loss for the NCE was Baltia’s next gen industry: body augmentation.

Baltia was considered the center of technological development inside the NCE. Almost all new advances related with cyberization and NInternet (New Internet) came from Baltian companies and industries. The large international support for Baltia’s cause was, in part, related to this. If the country was independent, anybody could buy these technologies without having to deal with the NCE. 

Once Baltia was free from NCE’s control, the civil and military markets were flooded with affordable and excellent quality cyber augmentations and prosthetics. More and more people, due to health conditions or hazardous occupations, or just mere curiosity or vanity, decided to augment parts or even their whole bodies. 

Most, if not all members of Geist have some sort of augmentation. New recruits are offered basic cyberization kits, military grade, so they can expand their abilities if needed. 

What kind of augmentation would you like to have?

notes.title: Characters and World Context: Ellen Verstek
notes.content:
All members of the Geist Unit (GU) actively participated in the Liberation War, which lasted five years. Some of them had to join the fight to protect their loved ones. Others jumped in by pure conviction. But none came unscathed.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/fb6b3ac499925c4c484edd6724fcbf48d3857c6a.jpg[/img]


[b]Ellen Verstek [/b]could be defined as a “child soldier”. Something as inhuman as this could easily break a young person, but Ellen was strong enough to endure the battles. Starting with logistical and communications duties, Ellen was quickly assigned to field tasks as part of a sabotage unit, disrupting NCE comms and ambushing enemy recon teams. Daughter of Ignatius Verstek and Leena Marev, Ellen was named [i][b]“the silent witch”[/b][/i] by the end of the war, due to her ability to blend with the environment and score silent kills. She briefly met [b]Marcus [/b]and [b]Borko [/b]during the war, and by the end of it, age 18, Ellen was scouted by [b]Daumantas [/b]and began an elite training program. She was to be the leader of the first Geist Unit.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34265206/e6074a8b583b495f33d9da0e7dc9348b60aefbcc.jpg[/img]

Are you ready to be Ellen's guardian angel?

notes.title: Cyber Ops: Characters and World Context
notes.content:
When creating Cyber Ops (CO), we knew that, for a game to succeed, having excellent graphics and mechanics is not enough. We wanted the protagonists to feel somewhat real, with motivations and experiences that could drive their journey through the game.

We love the concept of Special Units. A group of soldiers, well trained and focused, usually under a competent command, trying to complete mission objectives against all odds. And there is no other unit more iconic for us than Section 9, from the GITS universe. But even this powerful elite group had to accept the politics and machinations coming from the Government. And usually, their human side was what made them as memorable as they were.

The members of the Geist Division have their own stories. All of them were part of the Liberation War against the NCE, a large nation looking to maintain its former geopolitical power. When your enemy is that powerful, you can expect the war to be brutal and merciless. The stories of the cast try to reflect on that. Sometimes, there are no “correct” choices. Sometimes, you have to do what you have to do.

What's your main motivation to join our battle? Tell us in the comments ;)

notes.title: Cyber Ops: Dev Blog update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34265206/50236610a2821163b0bb361894daed2f25ea129d.png[/img]

It has been a long (but fun!) process for us in developing CO, so we want to share part of it with you! So, we will start making regular “dev-blog” like updates, until the game releases.

Many people ask us “why did you choose this retro-style design”? Well, there are several reasons. Even though we contemplated the idea of generating more detailed assets during the design phase, we chose the current CO look and feel for its stylistic value. We love the cyberpunk aesthetics, so for us it was logical to take inspiration from masterpieces like Blade Runner and the original Ghost in the Shell movie, to name a few (the original Alien is another one). The mixture of a futuristic world with retro style computers and interfaces (in the case of GITS it was more due to the early stages of CGI development) provides the user with a nostalgic feeling, and we wanted to convey that to the player.

What do you think about the visual style? Let us know in the comments! :)

notes.title: Hello there, Cyber Operators!!
notes.content:
We are thrilled to reveal [b]Cyber Ops: Tactical Hacking Support[/b]!!, our own take on mission support simulation.

This project can be traced back to 2017, where it all started with a few simple questions... 

- How would a stealth game like Metal Gear or Splinter Cell look from the perspective of the people in charge of radio/satellite support? 
- How can we create a bond with the agents on the other end of the line?
- How can we make this new perspective a challenging and engaging experience? 

With Cyber Ops, we are looking to provide an answer for these questions by creating a deep, real-time experience where real agents depend on you to complete their missions and get back to base in one piece.

Our take is a story-based novel experience, where you will assist the top agents of Baltia's Geist Division; strong characters facing complex missions in a tech-noir cyberpunk world. 

Political intrigue, conspirations, high-tech body upgrades, brain hacking, mechs, synths and everything we love about movies like Ghost in the Shell, Blade Runner, Escape from New York, Alien and more. 

We really hope you like the vibe of Cyber Ops. We are a passionate team and this is the kind of game we've been wanting to make for a long time, so we are giving our best to deliver the coolest cyberpunk experience you can get in 2019 ;)

Feel free to post any questions or feedback! We're looking forward to talk with you!

Thank you all,

Julio Marambio
Octeto Studios
CEO and Game Designer
